$comment: Docs table of contents. Read by src/lib/docs.ts (routes, nav, metadata) and scripts/prepare.mjs (Markdown mirrors). `file` is relative to the repo root. `metaTitle` stays under 45 characters so the page title with the ' · Tomato Player' suffix fits in 60. `description` is answer-first, 120 to 160 characters.

items.title: Getting started
items.metaTitle: Getting started: install and first player
items.description: Install Tomato Player from npm or the CDN, create your first video player with a skin, add HLS streaming and plugins, and use it in React, Vue or Svelte.

items.title: Architecture
items.metaTitle: Architecture of a modular video player
items.description: How Tomato Player is built: a dependency-free core with a state store, providers for playback engines, and separate skins, plugins and framework bindings.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.description: Fixes for common Tomato Player problems: blocked autoplay, play() errors, iPhone fullscreen, NO_PROVIDER, cross-origin captions, SSR hydration and strict CSP.

items.title: Migration
items.metaTitle: Migrate from Plyr, Video.js or Vidstack
items.description: Migration guides that map Plyr, Video.js, Vidstack and ReactPlayer options, events and APIs to their Tomato Player equivalents, with code side by side.

items.title: Skins
items.description: Tomato Player ships nine swappable skins. Pick one, pass its options, theme it with --tp-* design tokens and CSS state attributes, or switch it at runtime.

items.title: Plugins
items.description: Tomato Player plugins add hotkeys, touch gestures, chapters, seek thumbnails, playlists, QoE analytics, Media Session and saved settings. Options and usage.

items.title: Streaming (HLS & DASH)
items.metaTitle: HLS and DASH streaming, live and DRM
items.description: Stream HLS with hls.js and MPEG-DASH with dash.js in Tomato Player. Both engines load lazily. Covers quality switching, live and DVR, and DRM configuration.

items.title: React, Vue & Svelte
items.metaTitle: React, Vue, Svelte video player setup
items.description: Use Tomato Player in React and Next.js, Vue and Nuxt, Svelte and SvelteKit, or any framework through the <tomato-player> web component. SSR-safe bindings.

items.title: Accessibility
items.description: Tomato Player targets WCAG 2.2 AA in every official skin: labelled buttons and sliders, visible focus, captions, a full keyboard map and reduced-motion support.

items.title: Custom skins guide
items.metaTitle: Custom video player skins: full guide
items.description: The complete guide to Tomato Player skins: theme with tokens, override CSS safely, build a skin from UI primitives, test it and publish it to npm. With example.

items.title: Create a skin
items.metaTitle: Create a skin in the monorepo
items.description: The short workflow for adding a skin to the Tomato Player monorepo: scaffold it with pnpm new, compose controls with createSkin, scope the CSS and validate it.

items.title: Create a plugin
items.description: Write a Tomato Player plugin with definePlugin: a setup() function that uses the player API and events, returns a typed API and cleans up everything it starts.

items.title: Create a provider
items.description: Providers connect Tomato Player to a playback engine or platform such as Shaka, mpegts.js or an iframe API. Implement canPlay and create, and lazy-load it.

items.title: Player API
items.description: Reference for createPlayer in Tomato Player: every option with its default, the state object, methods such as seek and setSkin, typed events and error codes.

items.title: UI primitives
items.metaTitle: UI primitives for video player skins
items.description: Reference for @tomato-player/ui: accessible buttons, sliders, menus, overlays, captions and layout helpers that every Tomato Player skin is built from.

items.title: Roadmap
items.description: What shipped in Tomato Player 0.1 and what comes next, prioritised from the research collection: P0 items first, then P1 and exploratory P2 work.

items.title: Changelog
items.description: Release notes for Tomato Player. Version 0.1.0 is the first public release: core engine, UI primitives, nine skins, eight plugins, HLS and DASH, bindings.

items.title: Contributing
items.description: How to contribute to Tomato Player: set up the monorepo, scaffold skins and plugins, run the build, tests, validation and size checks, and open a pull request.

items.title: Security
items.description: Tomato Player security policy: which versions receive fixes during 0.x, how to report a vulnerability privately through GitHub advisories, and scope notes.

items.title: Code of conduct
items.description: Tomato Player follows the Contributor Covenant 2.1. Be welcoming and respectful in issues, pull requests and discussions, and report problems privately.

items.title: Overview
items.description: Research behind Tomato Player, with sources linked inline: the player landscape, developer pain points, opportunities and the third-party integration strategy.

items.title: Player landscape
items.description: A sourced snapshot of 14 web video players and engines plus 12 building blocks, comparing license, latest version, maintenance status and bundle size.

items.title: Developer pain points
items.metaTitle: Developer pain points with video players
items.description: Fourteen recurring problems developers report with web video players, each with linked evidence from issues and docs and the Tomato Player design decision.

items.title: Opportunities
items.description: Opportunities and differentiators for a new web video player, ranked P0 to P2 against what Video.js 10 and other players already ship, with sources.

items.title: Integration strategy
items.description: How Tomato Player integrates hls.js, dash.js and other engines: optional peer dependencies behind provider and plugin interfaces, loaded only when needed.
